formulations.text: For a measurable space (Ω,F), a discrete-time filtration is a family (F_n)_{n≥0} of sub-σ-algebras of F such that F_n⊆F_m whenever n≤m.

context: Conditional expectation with respect to a sub-sigma-algebra
editorial_screening_reason: ProofWiki defines the σ-algebra-conditioned conditional expectation by integrability, G-measurability and matching integrals over each event A∈G; essential uniqueness is a separate theorem. The object is a random variable defined up to almost-sure equality, not a single number. Martingale equations are equality almost surely of such conditional expectation versions. This is not the simpler discrete expectation conditioned on a single positive-probability event. The essential uniqueness statement is separately a theorem, intentionally omitted from the displayed definition.

formulations.text: For an integrable real random variable X on (Ω,F,P) and a sub-σ-algebra G⊆F, a version of E[X|G] is an integrable G-measurable random variable Z satisfying ∫_A Z dP = ∫_A X dP for every A∈G.

context: Proper vertex coloring of a simple undirected graph
editorial_screening_reason: The accessible ProofWiki Proper Vertex Coloring page explicitly defines the mapping to a palette of k colors and requires adjacent vertices receive unequal colors. The palette may have unused colors, and this is a vertex-coloring concept distinct from edge coloring. The chromatic number is the minimum k that admits such a coloring, so the source-screened proper coloring meaning will provide an exact noncircular prerequisite when separately reviewed.

formulations.text: A proper vertex k-coloring of a simple graph G=(V,E) is a map c:V→{1,…,k} such that c(u)≠c(v) for every edge {u,v}∈E.

context: General measurable-state-valued stochastic process indexed by a set
editorial_screening_reason: The accessible ProofWiki formal definition allows an arbitrary index set and measurable state space. Sequences indexed by nonnegative integers and real-time indexed processes are special cases. The state-space measurability requirement is essential; merely taking an arbitrary family of functions without measurability would not satisfy the usual definition. Adaptedness is a separate property relative to a filtration.

formulations.text: For a probability space (Ω,F,P), a measurable state space (E,Ecal), and an index set I, a stochastic process is an I-indexed family (X_i)_{i∈I} of E-valued random variables on Ω.
